title: Tomasz Kosowski sentenced to death after representing himself in capital murder trial | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

A man who defended himself in his capital murder case and refused a jury trial will face execution in Florida, a judge decided Friday.

In a rare and largely unprecedented move for a death penalty case,Tomasz Kosowski represented himselfand waived his right to a jury trial, leaving a judge in Pinellas County, Florida, to decide his fate.

Prosecutors presented the state’s case over six days in September, laying out for the judge how the former plastic surgeon accosted a lawyer, Steven Cozzi, in the bathroom of his office building on a Tuesday morning in 2023. Cozzi, whose law firm was involved in contentious civil litigation with Kosowski at the time, was never seen again.

At a brief sentencing hearing Friday, the judge handed the parties a prewritten sentencing ruling, then announced his decision to order Kosowski’s death.

“The court concludes that the defendant, under the laws of the state of Florida, has forfeited his right to live,” Judge Joseph Bulone said in court Friday afternoon. “Accordingly, it is ordered and adjudged that the defendant Tomasz Kosowski is sentenced to death for the murder of Steven Cozzi.”

Kosowski, who dismissed his court-appointed criminalattorneys weeks before the trial, did not present a case in his defense.

He did offer a closing argument, speaking directly to the judge to suggest prosecutors did not prove the statutory elements of first-degree murder. In a soft voice, leaning into the microphone, Kosowski spoke for about 20 minutes, about the lack of a body or a death certificate for Cozzi.

Kosowski, 47, also declined to present a case in the penalty phase and offered no mitigation materials or statements to support sparing his life.

The judge appointed independent special counsel to present mitigating materials about Kosowski to support a life sentence over the death penalty.

The attorney told the court about Kosowski’s upbringing as a Polish immigrant who moved with his parents to Kansas in his youth and how the Ivy League-educated doctor could help other inmates in prison. No witnesses took the stand on Kosowski’s behalf.

Bulone acknowledged some mitigating factors in Kosowski’s favor but said they’re outweighed especially by the “cold and calculated” manner by which Kosowski murdered Cozzi.

“The court has given great weight to the aggravating factor that the homicide was committed in a cold, calculated, and premeditated manner, without any pretense of moral or legal justification,” Bulone said at the sentencing.

At the start of the sentencing, Kosowski presented a motion to disqualify the judge, leading Bulone to adjourn the hearing briefly to review it. The judge returned to the bench minutes later without addressing the motion.

Prosecutors had highlighted the premeditation that went into Cozzi’s murder as an aggravating factor to support putting Kosowski to death.

In 2019, Kosowski sued former colleagues over a billing dispute, and in 2022 he started representing himself, putting him in direct dealings with the other doctors’ attorneys – including Cozzi.

Kosowski expressed animus toward Cozzi as the civil proceedings stretched on for years, prosecutors said at trial.

The plastic surgeon researched Cozzi online, drove to his home and surveilled the law firm’s office several times in the months before he killed Cozzi, trial evidence showed.

Cozzi became an “obsession” for Kosowski, Assistant State Attorney Nathan Vonderheide said during closing arguments.

On March 21, 2023, Cozzi went to the restroom down the hall from his office, leaving an email draft open and music playing from his phone.

He never returned to his desk.

Prosecutors allege Kosowski waited in the bathroom for the lawyer and killed him there before dragging Cozzi’s body out of the building in a cart.

Surveillance footage shows a man enter the building and hours later – wearing different clothes – drag a cart toward the parking lot.

Kosowski joined a 10:30 a.m. virtual hearing for their mutual case from the law firm parking lot, minutes after getting Cozzi’s body out of the building, according to prosecutors.

The doctor moved for sanctions against Cozzi, seeking to remove the lawyer from the case, but Cozzi wasn’t on the call, prompting other firm members to look for him and report his disappearance.

After a stop at his waterfront home, Kosowski took Cozzi’s body to a dumpster on a remote road nearly four hours away, trial evidence showed, then continued to Miami where he performed scheduled surgeries the next day.

Investigators were too late to recover any evidence of Cozzi – the dumpster contents had already been taken to a landfill.

Kosowski was the only person known to have a problem with Cozzi, the lawyer’s husband and colleagues told law enforcement at the time, quickly making the surgeon a person of interest in Cozzi’s disappearance.

Kosowski was arrested four days after the killing with nearly $300,000 in cash, two passports and a “murder bag” in his trunk, prosecutors said at trial.

Video of the arrest shown in court captured the doctor in the back of a squad car sucking meticulously on each of his fingers after he wriggled his cuffed wrists from behind his body underneath his feet and into his lap.He also had several bruises and scrapes all over his body, photos shown in court revealed.

Cozzi’s blood was found in the bed of Kosowski’s pickup truck and on a ballistic vest in the trunk of Kosowski’s second car, DNA results submitted at trial confirmed.
